problems.stem: A lesson begins with thirty minutes of new content with no statement of what learners are expected to do at the end. Which Gagné event is missing?
options: Event 2: Inform Learners of the Objective
problems.explanation: Without an explicit objective, learners cannot mobilize the right strategies or self-monitor. This is the missing event 2.

problems.stem: What is the cognitive purpose of Event 3 — Stimulate Recall of Prior Learning?
options: To create warm-up trivia so learners are entertained.
To deliberately retrieve schemas from long-term memory so the new content has somewhere to attach in working memory.
To delay the start of the lesson.
To replace the need for assessment.
problems.explanation: Stimulating recall is a deliberate retrieval move. Without active prior knowledge, the new content has no schema to attach to.

problems.stem: An online lesson asks learners to click 'I understand' and paraphrase the rule. Why is this not Event 6 — Elicit Performance?
options: It is fine; paraphrasing is performance.
Performance means attempting the actual behavior the objective specifies, not paraphrasing or acknowledging.
Event 6 only applies to physical skills.
Paraphrase is the same as practice in cognitive learning.
problems.explanation: Eliciting performance means attempting the objective's verb. Paraphrasing or clicking 'I understand' is metacognitive talk, not the performance.

problems.stem: Learners score 90% on the in-lesson assessment but cannot apply the skill the following week. Which Gagné event is most likely missing or weak?
options: Event 2: Inform Learners of the Objective
problems.explanation: High in-session score with poor downstream transfer is the classic signature of a missing or weak Event 9.
